items.name: RNA-Seq Differential Expression Analysis
items.iwc_workflow_name: RNA-Seq Differential Expression Analysis with Visualization
items.query:
Using the provided raw count tables and two-condition design, perform a standard differential-expression analysis for raw count data, comparing the changed condition against the reference condition.
Before testing, retain a gene only when it has at least 10 raw counts in at least two of the four samples. Test every retained gene and no others.
Report an unshrunken log2 fold change for each retained gene, positive when expression is higher in the changed condition, together with a raw p-value and a Benjamini-Hochberg adjusted p-value computed across the retained genes.
Write `final_answer/differential_expression.tsv` with exactly four tab-separated columns named `gene_id`, `log2_fold_change`, `p_value` and `fdr`. Include one row for every retained gene and no other rows, and do not remove rows by significance. Use the gene identifiers exactly as they appear in the input count tables. Every log2 fold change must be finite, and every p-value and adjusted p-value must lie between 0 and 1.
Write `final_answer/method.json` as a JSON object with a single key `method` whose value is the common name of the differential-expression method you used.

evaluator.description: Continuous per-gene agreement over the fixed prefiltered gene universe. Reported as five separate components combined by geometric mean: gene-set coverage, fold-change direction on effect-bearing genes, fold-change magnitude by Lin's concordance correlation coefficient, fold-change ranking, and the ranking of statistical evidence. Magnitude deliberately is not a correlation - correlation is invariant to multiplying every fold change by a constant, and CCC is not.

items.name: Paired-End Amplicon Denoising
items.iwc_workflow_name: Dada2: amplicon analysis for paired end data
items.query:
Denoise the provided primer-free, paired-end 16S rRNA V4 reads into exact amplicon sequence variants. The reads are 2x250 bp Illumina MiSeq data from 17 mouse caecal samples sequenced in one run. Use the paired-end information to reconstruct the full amplicons and remove chimeras de novo.
Write `final_answer/asv_abundance.tsv` as a tab-separated raw-count table. The first column must be named `sequence` and contain uppercase ASV nucleotide sequences in the orientation of the provided forward reads. Every remaining column must correspond to exactly one input sample and use its supplied identifier, with no missing, additional, or renamed samples. Include one row per unique ASV and report nonnegative raw counts, not relative abundance.

evaluator.description: Geometric mean of two parts. Detection is precision/recall F1 over the set of variants, counted without abundance weighting. Abundance is abundance-weighted F1 over the per-sample counts. Variants are aligned by their nucleotide sequence, compared exactly and uppercased, because an amplicon sequence variant is defined by its exact sequence - two sequences differing by one nucleotide are distinct ASVs, not one spelled two ways, although ASVs do not correspond one to one with organisms or species. Samples are aligned by identifier, so column order is free.

criteria.requirement: Read-quality evidence was inspected before or during parameter selection.
Filtering/truncation parameters are recorded, retain nondegenerate data, and preserve sufficient expected V4 overlap.
Forward/reverse files remain correctly paired within every sample.

criteria.requirement: Denoised forward and reverse variants were merged by sequence overlap.

criteria.requirement: A de-novo chimera detector was run on the merged sequence table.

items.name: Antimicrobial Resistance Determinant Detection
items.query:
Identify the antimicrobial resistance determinants carried by the provided complete `Escherichia coli` genome. Report both acquired resistance genes and resistance-conferring chromosomal point mutations.
Identify acquired genes using ResFinder release `d1e607b` and point mutations using PointFinder release `694919f`, with `Escherichia coli` as the PointFinder organism. Write `final_answer/resistance_determinants.tsv` as a tab-separated table with a header and a first column named `determinant`, one determinant per row. Use the database names for acquired genes. Represent a point mutation as the gene followed by the substitution, for example `gyrA (S83L)`. Do not include plasmid replicons or multilocus sequence types.

items.name: Single-Cell Pseudobulk Aggregation
items.iwc_workflow_name: Single-Cell Pseudobulk Differential Expression Analysis with edgeR
items.query:
Aggregate the provided annotated single-cell RNA-seq data into pseudobulk profiles, then test those profiles for differential expression between the two disease groups.
Use the raw counts in the AnnData layer `counts`. Sum counts by `individual` and `cell_type`, and retain only individual-cell-type combinations containing at least 10 cells.
Filter the retained pseudobulk samples to expressed genes as follows. Let N be the number of retained samples and M the median of their total counts, and let S = ceil(10 + 0.7 x (N - 10)). Compute each gene's counts per million within each sample using that sample's own total count. Retain a gene only when its counts per million is at least 10 / M x 1,000,000 in at least S samples, and its summed count across all retained samples is at least 1,000. Apply this rule once to all retained samples together, without reference to the disease groups.
Write `final_answer/pseudobulk_counts.tsv` as a tab-separated raw-count matrix with one row per retained gene. The first column must be named `gene` and contain the `gene_symbol` values. Include exactly one column for each retained individual-cell-type combination and no other pseudobulk columns. Name these columns `<individual>_<cell_type>`, replacing every space and hyphen with an underscore. Each matrix entry must be the summed nonnegative integer raw count. Row and column order do not matter.
Then test every gene in that filtered matrix for differential expression between the disease groups, using a standard count-based negative-binomial differential-expression method and a model that accounts for both disease and cell type. Use the normal-minus-COVID-19 contrast, so a positive log2 fold change means higher expression in normal. Report unshrunken log2 fold changes.
Write `final_answer/differential_expression.tsv` with exactly four tab-separated columns named `gene`, `log2_fold_change`, `p_value` and `fdr`. Use the same gene identifiers as `final_answer/pseudobulk_counts.tsv`. Include one row for every gene in that matrix and no other rows, and do not remove rows by significance. Every log2 fold change must be finite, and every p-value and adjusted p-value must lie between 0 and 1. Report finite numeric `p_value` and `fdr` values for every gene. Do not omit a gene or report a missing value because your method flags it as an outlier. Report the adjusted p-value as a Benjamini-Hochberg adjustment of your own p-values across those genes.
Write `final_answer/method.json` as a JSON object with a single key `method` whose value is the common name of the differential-expression method you used.

evaluator.description: Two artifacts scored separately and combined as their geometric mean. The pseudobulk matrix keeps the scorer it has always had, because it is exactly reproducible and nothing about it changed. The differential-expression table is scored continuously against the calibrated reference for the declared method. Both components are always reported.

items.name: BioProject Metadata and Sequence Retrieval
items.iwc_workflow_name: Metadata and Sequences from BioProject IDs
items.query:
Retrieve the run-level metadata and biological sequence reads for every currently public SRA run associated with the BioProject accessions listed in the input file. Exclude technical reads, preserve each run's `SINGLE` or `PAIRED` layout, and do not alter the biological read sequences or quality strings after retrieval.
Under `final_answer/metadata/`, write exactly one table for each input BioProject at `final_answer/metadata/<ACCESSION>.tsv`. Each table must contain exactly one row for every run of that BioProject, and every row's `bioproject` value must equal `<ACCESSION>`. Each table must contain at least the following columns: `bioproject`, `run_accession`, `study_accession`, `experiment_accession`, `sample_accession`, `biosample`, `organism_taxid`, `organism_name`, `library_strategy`, `library_source`, `library_selection`, `library_layout`, `instrument_model`, `run_total_spots`, and `run_total_bases`. Additional columns are allowed.
Write `final_answer/run_manifest.tsv` with at least the columns `bioproject`, `run_accession`, `library_layout`, `forward_path`, and `reverse_path`. Column order does not matter and additional columns are allowed. Include every run exactly once, and describe the same run set as the metadata tables.
For paired-end runs, set `library_layout` to `PAIRED` and provide synchronized forward and reverse FASTQ paths. For single-end runs, set `library_layout` to `SINGLE`, provide the FASTQ path in `forward_path`, and leave `reverse_path` empty. All paths must be relative to `final_answer/`.
Store all retrieved FASTQ files under `final_answer/reads/` and reference them from the manifest.

evaluator.description:
Geometric mean of three independently reported components.
`project_run_layout_f1` is an F1 over (bioproject, run_accession, library_layout) triples, so filing a run under the wrong project costs the same as missing it.
`metadata_f1` is an F1 over (run_accession, field, normalized_value) triples restricted to the fifteen stable fields listed below and stated in the query.
`exact_run_content_f1` is an F1 over runs, not over reads. Each expected run is one binary unit: its whole (sequence, quality) multiset must match the stored fingerprint, and there is no partial credit inside a run. The name says so deliberately - an earlier draft described this as read-level F1, which it is not. A run only half retrieved is a failed retrieval, not a differently shaped scientific answer, and a truncated run therefore costs exactly what a wholly wrong one does.

steps.requirement: Read the BioProject accessions and retrieve run-level metadata for every input project.

criteria.requirement: Every input BioProject accession was read and queried against a public run-level metadata source.
Retrieved metadata covers every public run selected for each project with required fields.

steps.requirement: Build the complete, deduplicated set of public run accessions while preserving project and layout information.

criteria.requirement: The selected run-accession set is complete for the retrieved public metadata snapshot and contains no duplicates.
Every selected run retains its BioProject and SINGLE/PAIRED layout association.

steps.requirement: Retrieve the biological reads for every run and exclude technical reads.

criteria.requirement: Biological FASTQ reads were successfully retrieved for every selected public run.
Technical reads were excluded by the retrieval mode or an explicit technical-read filter.
Retrieved FASTQ files are readable and consistent with run-level spots/bases or checksums when available.

steps.requirement: Separate paired-end and single-end outputs and keep paired mates synchronized.

criteria.requirement: SINGLE runs have one forward file and no reverse file; PAIRED runs have both mate files.
Every paired FASTQ has matching record counts and synchronized mate identifiers.

steps.requirement: Produce one metadata table per BioProject and a manifest linking each project, run, and layout to the correct FASTQ paths, with metadata and manifest describing the same runs.

criteria.requirement: Exactly one required metadata table exists per input BioProject with the required schema.
The manifest paths resolve to the correct SINGLE or PAIRED FASTQ files for every run.
Metadata and manifest contain exactly the same project-run set and pass final-answer checks.
